summary: Raimond Gaita is a philosopher who earned degrees from the University of Melbourne and Leeds (PhD). He taught at King's College London (Professor of Moral Philosophy, 1977–2011) and Australian Catholic University (Foundation Professor of Philosophy, 1993–2011).

Historian and archaeologist Rajan Gurukkal studied at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and Sundararajan Visiting Professor at the Indian Institute of Science (2012–2016).

Indologist Rajendra Chandra Hazra completed his BA at the University of Dhaka and doctoral research under Sushil Kumar De. His career included lectureships at Jagannath University and Dhaka, followed by an associate professorship at Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Indologist and historian Rajendralal Mitra studied at Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He directed Wards' Institution (1856–1881) and held positions at The Asiatic Society as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885).
Historian Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University. He later held academic posts at Presidency University and Scottish Church College.

Historian and Indologist Rakhal Das Banerji studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He served as an officer with the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and held a professorship of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Gendün Chöphel and Trijang Rinpoche.

Tibetologist Ralf Kramer studied under David P. Jackson, earning an MA at the University of Hamburg before studying at the University of London. Around 2004, he was the Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Library.

Philosopher Ralph Abraham earned his BSE, Master's, and doctorate from the University of Michigan and studied under Debabrata Sensharma. After teaching at Columbia and Princeton, he became an Associate Professor (1968) and Professor (1980) at the University of California, Santa Cruz.
Philosopher Ralph Lerner studied at the University of Chicago under Leo Strauss (~1947–1953). He subsequently held a faculty post at the University of Chicago from around 1953 to 2003.

Indologist and linguist Ralph Lilley Turner studied at Christ's College. He served as Professor of Indian Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922) and as Director of SOAS University of London (1922–1957).

Indologist Ralph T. H. Griffith studied under Horace Hayman Wilson at The Queen's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (~1853–1885) and was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1861–1878).
Philosopher Ralph Waldo Emerson completed his studies at Harvard College (~1817–1821) and Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826).

Archaeologist and Indologist Ram Chandra Kak studied at Sri Pratap College and trained under John Marshall. He was superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1914–1929) and Director of the Department of Archæology and Research for Jammu and Kashmir (1919–1929).

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned his MA at Patna University and his PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He served as vice chancellor at Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, Ram Mohan Roy founded several institutions, including the Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), the Anglo-Hindu School (1822), the Vedanta College (1826), and the Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Ram Niwas Pandey, a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, completing doctoral research under Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Shankar Tripathi worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Head of the Department of Bauddhadarśana at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998) and as Dean of the Faculty of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Historian and Indologist Ram Sharan Sharma earned his PhD at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He headed Patna University's History Department (1958–1973), chaired the Indian Council of Historical Research (1972–1977), and was professor and dean at the University of Delhi (1973–1978).

Indologist and linguist Rama Nath Sharma studied under Raghunath Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi, earning degrees from Allahabad, Agra, and Rochester (PhD). He served as Professor at the University of Rochester (1971–1976) and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1976–2012).
